display_title: jax.scipy.fft.idct: compute the inverse with irfft instead of ifft

head_commit.message:
jax.scipy.fft.idct: compute the inverse with irfft instead of ifft

`idct` built a full-length complex spectrum and ran a complex-to-complex
`ifft`, then discarded the imaginary part. Since the coefficients are
real, only the Hermitian part of the spectrum matters, and it can be
assembled directly at half length -- a real-to-complex transform then
does half the FFT work. `_dct_deinterleave` is also rewritten as a
stack + reshape instead of a zero-fill plus two strided scatters.

Up to 2.7x faster on GPU and 9.4x on CPU for batched inputs; max
absolute difference vs the previous implementation is 3e-8 (float32).

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [linalg] Fix eigh JVP division-by-zero on degenerate spectra and add precision tests (follow-up to #40149)

head_commit.message:
[linalg] Fix eigh JVP division-by-zero on degenerate spectra and add precision tests

PR #40149 resolved the large-eigenvalue mantissa cliff by computing eigenvalue differences prior to reciprocal calculation (Fmat = (delta_w + eye_n)^(-1) - eye_n). However, for degenerate spectra (repeated eigenvalues), off-diagonal entries have delta_w == 0 and eye_n == 0, causing integer_pow(0, -1) to evaluate to inf.

This patch masks all zero eigenvalue differences (delta_w == 0, spanning both the diagonal and degenerate off-diagonal pairs) to 1 before inverting:
delta_w = lax.select(delta_w == 0, lax.full_like(delta_w, 1), delta_w)
Fmat = lax.integer_pow(delta_w, -1) - eye_n

This preserves finite invariant subspace tangents for degenerate spectra, keeps exact zero on the diagonal, adds shared helpers in jax/_src/test_util.py, and adds 5 parameterized test methods in tests/lax_test.py and tests/linalg_test.py covering cliffs, ill-conditioned matrices, and degenerate spectra.

display_title: Prefix private imports with underscores in jax.numpy type stubs

head_commit.message:

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Fix complex `dot_general` with an explicit dot algorithm dropping the imaginary part

head_commit.message:
Fix complex `dot_general` with an explicit dot algorithm dropping the imaginary part

`dot_general` with complex operands and a `DotAlgorithmPreset` or
`DotAlgorithm` (passed as `precision=` or set through
`jax_default_matmul_precision`) returned `Re(lhs) @ Re(rhs)`. It gave no error
or warning. `get_algorithm_compute_types` maps any operand dtype that the
algorithm does not list to the algorithm's real storage type, e.g. `complex64`
to `float32`. `_handle_dot_precision` then emits a `complex -> real`
`convert`, which keeps only the real part.

XLA's dot algorithms are only defined for real operands (see
`IsSupportedDotAlgorithmOnGpu` in `xla/service/algorithm_util.cc`), so we cannot
pass a complex element type through with the algorithm. Instead,
`_dot_general_lower` now lowers complex dots with an explicit algorithm as real
dots on the real and imaginary parts, as the issue suggests:

* Each real dot uses the requested algorithm. The dots and their sums use the
  algorithm's accumulation type, and only the result is cast to the output
  type. So a narrower `preferred_element_type` does not truncate the inputs or
  the partial sums.
* Both operands use the wider of their real input types, so a narrower real
  operand (e.g. `bfloat16 @ complex64`) does not lower the precision of the
  complex operand.
* A real operand needs 2 real dots instead of 4, and a real
  `preferred_element_type` only computes the real part.

The decomposition only happens at lowering time, so jaxprs, autodiff and
batching rules are unchanged. Real operands, `DEFAULT`, `ANY_F8_*`,
`precision=None` and `lax.Precision` take the same path as before. Raising an
error instead would break complex programs that run under a global preset
`jax_default_matmul_precision` for their real matmuls.

`_handle_dot_precision` now raises a `ValueError` instead of casting a complex
operand to a real type. This covers `ragged_dot_general` lowered to
`chlo.ragged_dot` on TPU/GPU, which also calls `_handle_dot_precision`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42329

`IsSupportedDotAlgorithmOnGpu` in `xla/service/algorithm_util.cc`), so we cannot
pass a complex element type through with the algorithm. Instead,
`_dot_general_lower` now lowers complex dots with an explicit algorithm as real
dots on the real and imaginary parts, as the issue suggests:

* Each real dot uses the requested algorithm. The dots and their sums use the
  algorithm's accumulation type, and only the result is cast to the output
  type. So a narrower `preferred_element_type` does not truncate the inputs or
  the partial sums.
* Both operands use the wider of their real input types, so a narrower real
  operand (e.g. `bfloat16 @ complex64`) does not lower the precision of the
  complex operand.
* A real operand needs 2 real dots instead of 4, and a real
  `preferred_element_type` only computes the real part.

The decomposition only happens at lowering time, so jaxprs, autodiff and
batching rules are unchanged. Real operands, `DEFAULT`, `ANY_F8_*`,
`precision=None` and `lax.Precision` take the same path as before. Raising an
error instead would break complex programs that run under a global preset
`jax_default_matmul_precision` for their real matmuls.

`_handle_dot_precision` now raises a `ValueError` instead of casting a complex
operand to a real type. This covers `ragged_dot_general` lowered to
`chlo.ragged_dot` on TPU/GPU, which also calls `_handle_dot_precision`.

head_commit.message:
[jax] Fix coo_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

When `nse` exceeds the number of nonzeros, `_coo_fromdense_impl` pads `row` and `col` with `(0, 0)` (the default `fill_value` of `jnp.nonzero`) and masks the padded `data` entries to zero. `_coo_fromdense_jvp` did not apply the same mask, so `_coo_extract(row, col, Mdot)` gave every padded entry a tangent of `Mdot[0, 0]` instead of zero. Mask `data_dot` with the same `true_nonzeros` mask used in `_coo_fromdense_impl`. The primal outputs, including the padded index values, are unchanged. Add a regression test that checks the JVP, gradient and Hessian with padded entries.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40624

head_commit.message:
Fix complex `dot_general` with an explicit dot algorithm dropping the imaginary part

`dot_general` with complex operands and a `DotAlgorithmPreset` or
`DotAlgorithm` (passed as `precision=` or set through
`jax_default_matmul_precision`) returned `Re(lhs) @ Re(rhs)`. It gave no error
or warning. `get_algorithm_compute_types` maps any operand dtype that the
algorithm does not list to the algorithm's real storage type, e.g. `complex64`

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [jax] Fix coo_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

head_commit.message:
[jax] Fix coo_fromdense JVP for padded entries when nse > nnz

When `nse` exceeds the number of nonzeros, `_coo_fromdense_impl` pads `row` and `col` with `(0, 0)` (the default `fill_value` of `jnp.nonzero`) and masks the padded `data` entries to zero. `_coo_fromdense_jvp` did not apply the same mask, so `_coo_extract(row, col, Mdot)` gave every padded entry a tangent of `Mdot[0, 0]` instead of zero. This produced wrong forward-mode tangents, wrong gradients (padded cotangents were scattered back into `M[0, 0]`), and wrong second derivatives.

Mask `data_dot` with the same `true_nonzeros` mask used in `_coo_fromdense_impl`. The primal outputs, including the padded index values, are unchanged. Add a regression test that checks the JVP, gradient and Hessian with padded entries.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/40624
